title: Reverse Linked List
statement: Given the `head` of a singly linked list, reverse the list and return the new head.

example.why: Every arrow now points the other way, so the old tail (3) is the new head.

idea: Each node only knows its `next`. Reversing the list means making every arrow point the other way.
Walk the list once with three pointers: `prev` (head of the part already reversed), `current` (the node being flipped) and `next_node` (a saved copy of the way forward).
For each node: **save** its next → **flip** its arrow back to `prev` → **slide** `prev` and `current` one step forward.

complexity.timeWhy: Each node is visited exactly once.
complexity.spaceWhy: Only three pointers are used, no matter how long the list is.

steps.text: Our example: **`head = [1,2,3]`**. Each step runs one highlighted line of the code.
`prev` is the head of the part that is **already reversed**. Nothing is reversed yet, so it starts as None.
`current` is the node we are about to flip. Start at the head, node 1.
We are about to overwrite `current.next`, so first **save** where it points: `next_node` = node 2. Without this we would lose the rest of the list.
**Flip the arrow**: node 1 now points back to None instead of forward.
Node 1 is now the head of the reversed part, so move `prev` onto it.
Step forward using the saved pointer: `current` = node 2.
We are about to overwrite `current.next`, so first **save** where it points: `next_node` = node 3. Without this we would lose the rest of the list.
**Flip the arrow**: node 2 now points back to node 1 instead of forward.
Node 2 is now the head of the reversed part, so move `prev` onto it.
Step forward using the saved pointer: `current` = node 3.
We are about to overwrite `current.next`, so first **save** where it points: `next_node` = None. Without this we would lose the rest of the list.
**Flip the arrow**: node 3 now points back to node 2 instead of forward.
Node 3 is now the head of the reversed part, so move `prev` onto it.
Step forward using the saved pointer: `current` = None.
`current` is None — we walked off the end, so every arrow has been flipped.
`prev` is on node 3, the new head. Return it.
Done — the answer is **`[3,2,1]`**. Every arrow now points the other way, so the old tail (3) is the new head.
